intro.TrustedMarkup:
The string predicates and slice, written on the byte view (bytes, s[i], stringFromBytes).

Offsets and lengths are bytes. A byte-wise scan is safe on UTF-8: a valid needle starts with an ASCII or a lead byte, so it cannot match at a continuation byte. The functions read the byteLength field, never byteLengthV: the field is O(1) and folds at compile time, while byteLengthV copies the string (4.5 ns against 72.5 ns on 47 bytes). The s.byteLength field as a function.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn startsWith(s: String, needle: String) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Does s begin with needle? An empty needle is a prefix of everything.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn endsWith(s: String, needle: String) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Does s end with needle? An empty needle is a suffix of everything.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn skipTable(needle: String, haystackBytes: Int64) -> Array<UInt32>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Boyer-Moore-Horspool's bad-character table for needle: for each byte, how far a window may jump when it ends on that byte. A plain Array, not a record: a field read per byte costs the interpreter measurably, and an array argument is shared copy-on-write.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn findPlain(s: String, needle: String, from: Int64 where value >= 0) -> Option<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first occurrence of needle at or after from, or None. A found offset is at most s.byteLength - needle.byteLength, so an empty needle occurs at from only when from <= s.byteLength. O(n*m).

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn worthPreparing(needle: String, haystackBytes: Int64) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether a table for needle pays over a haystack of that size. Callers ask before building the table: std/vyx calls contains on short strings millions of times, and an allocation per call cost it about 10%.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn findSkipping(s: String, needle: String, from: Int64 where value >= 0, skip: Array<UInt32> where value.length >= 256) -> Option<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: findPlain with a table from skipTable: it compares from the end of the window and, on a mismatch, skips by the table entry for the window's last byte, so it visits about n / m positions.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn contains(s: String, needle: String) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether needle occurs in s; an empty needle occurs everywhere.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type SliceError = enum { OutOfRange(Int64), SplitsCharacter(Int64) }

prose.TrustedMarkup: The two ways a byte range fails to name a substring, each carrying the offset that failed.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn slice(s: String, start: Int64, end: Int64) -> Result<String, SliceError>

prose.TrustedMarkup:
The bytes of s from start up to end, both byte offsets on UTF-8 character boundaries.

OutOfRange(start) when start < 0; OutOfRange(end) when end > s.byteLength or start > end. SplitsCharacter(i) when cut point i lands on a continuation byte. The range is checked before the boundary, as examples/strpredbytes.vyrn pins. A string that holds NUL, which no program can construct, returns SplitsCharacter(start).

It reads s[i] and s.byteLength, never bytes(s): std/scan slices once per token, so a whole-string copy per call would be quadratic.
